no_new_call_note: The live register is still empty, so there was nothing to review or post-mortem this week. On the hunt itself: every candidate found was already extensively covered by mainstream financial press before this week's search, not ahead of it. Fed Governor Waller's dovish remarks on September 3 (cooling inflation, openness to holding rates) were the lead story on every wire the same day and already moved yields, the dollar and equities before the search began. The Alphabet antitrust ruling on September 2 was instant front-page financial news, not a variant anyone could still be early on. The US-Iran conflict's knock-on effects - Strait of Hormuz tanker war-risk premiums near 10% of hull value, European gas at a fourth consecutive weekly gain, oil holding near $92 - are a running story dating to at least July, reported week after week by the mainstream press; the moves are behind us. Canada's retaliatory tariffs taking effect September 8 have been reported since August 25. The Panama Canal's transit cuts (36 to 34 ships daily from September 3, to 32 from September 15) have been the subject of dedicated consumer-facing reporting since August 20-21. Uranium supply tightness (Cameco and Kazatomprom production cuts) and rare-earth export-control enforcement are each multi-week running stories already priced by specialist and mainstream press alike. The Bank of Japan's expected September 17-18 hike is already the subject of Bloomberg, CNBC and Japan Times analysis with published market-implied odds - a calendar event already anticipated, not a variant against consensus. Junior-miner drill results (Kenorland, Aurum Resources, Power Minerals) are real and dated this week but are single-name speculative exploration stories without a quotable market consensus to disagree with, not a macro variant. Nothing found this week was simultaneously new, confirmed by more than one independent source, and still ahead of where the market's attention already sits - so no call was opened. An empty week is counted, not apologised for.
